content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV-cache resident set growth > 75% across inference-prod-usw2 pool. Multiple pods reporting OOMKill and 5xx rate spike. Auto-escalation to #eng-oncall.

maria: on it. paging @dan and @ashley for infra + kv cache logic. can someone confirm customer visible errors?

dan: got it, looking. seeing a sharp increase in continuous batching size across requests -> batch sizes hitting 512 for some sequences. KV key count jumped ~4x in last 10m.

ashley: oncall infra here. nodes in pool are flapping: kube events show OOMKilled on rtx nodes, pods restarting. HPA reacted, spawned new pods, they warm up then OOM again -> thrash.

maria: ok stop the HPA auto-scale to prevent thrash while we stabilize. applying temporary min replicas 6 and disable scale up.

ashley: patching HPA now:
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch hpa inference-prod --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":6},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/maxReplicas","value":8}]'
```

rachel: any idea what changed? I saw a config push 9m ago from deploy-bot for continuous-batch aggressive batching.

deploy-bot: Refs: deploy 2026-03-10T02:14Z by ops-team. Config key: runtime.continuous_batch.max_size=512 -> 512 (was 128).

maria: that matches. rollback the batching change to 128 as hotfix. @dan can you flip the runtime flag cluster-wide?

dan: rolling out flag rollback to inference-prod-usw2. Will push safe update with gradual rollout 25% -> 50% -> 100% to avoid instant load shift.

maria: given current OOMs we need faster: do a force rollout on the control plane flag for the entire pool, then scale HPA back appropriately.

ashley: manual eviction plan: drain one bad pod to let warm cache reconstruction happen on healthy pod. command I ran:
```bash
kubectl -n inference drain inference-prod-gg1-7 --ignore-daemonsets --force --delete-local-data
```

rachel: customer impact: monitoring shows elevated 5xx for dedicated clusters in us-west2 and hosted tenants on same pool. Estimated affected requests ~2.3k/min over last 7m. Not a full outage but significant degradation.

maria: severity: S3. paging policy: notify CSMs and post in #customer-impact. I'll prepare short message.

ashley: we should also evict large KV entries and tighten KV TTL to avoid rebuild surges. applying kv.ttl.default=30m (was 6h) as emergency.

dan: applying KV TTL change via runtime-config API:
```json
PATCH /v1/runtime-configs/inference-prod
{ "kv.default_ttl": "30m" }
```

maria: pause continuous batching on the pool while TTL takes effect.

rachel: sending heads-up to affected accounts now. message: "We're investigating elevated errors for some inferences in us-west2. Mitigations in progress; we'll update in 15m."

deploy-bot: flag rollback complete. runtime.continuous_batch.max_size -> 128. 100% rollout completed.

dan: seeing batch sizes drop to ~120-130 median. KV key growth leveling off. OOM events decreasing. Pod restarts down.

ashley: HPA is holding, no new scale-ups. but we still have a few stale caches that are large; memory pressure will relax over ~10-15m as TTL evictions happen.

maria: good. transition plan: keep HPA minReplicas at 6 for 20m then re-evaluate. continue to block new deploys to that pool for 30m.

rachel: CSMs acknowledged, some customers reported latency spikes but no data loss. capturing incident timeline for postmortem.

maria: quick root cause hypothesis: aggressive batch size bump caused KV cache to store many transient keys per request; combined with long KV TTL and immediate HPA scale-up caused a feedback loop: new pods warmed and stored more KV, memory grew, more OOMs, HPA further scaled -> thrash.

dan: agree. mitigations we did: 1) rollback batch size 2) lower KV TTL 3) set HPA min to avoid thrash 4) drain symptomatic pods 5) block new deploys.

ashley: follow-ups: add warmup delay on pod start to rate-limit initial KV writes, add cache write rate cap, and add HPA policy to avoid scaling on short CPU/memory spikes (increase evaluation window to 2m).

maria: creating a stub incident doc and assigning owners. please add notes: who changed batching (ops-team), timeline, customer impact numbers, commands executed.

dan: logging commands I ran into the thread for postmortem:
```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/inference-runtime --selector=pool=inference-prod-usw2
kubectl -n inference patch cm inference-runtime-config --patch '{"data":{"continuous_batch.max_size":"128"}}'
```

rachel: next steps for customer comms: follow-up status in 30m with ETA for full recovery.

maria: handoff: i'm on-call for another 25m then off. @dan, please take on second-line for remediation and postmortem. I'll remain reachable for 1h.

dan: taking handoff. I'll monitor metrics and start postmortem draft.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: errors trending down. 5xx rate returned to baseline ~22m after alerts. No new OOMs in last 8m.

maria: thanks team. create a retro ticket: infra-5007 KV-cache batching feedback loop. include suggested mitigations (warmup delay, write cap, config rollout guard rails).

ashley: adding HPA tweak PR to infra repo: increase targetAverageUtilization window -> 120s and add scaleDown stabilization windows.

rachel: posting final note to #customer-impact and tagging affected CSMs.

dan: leaving note: will add detailed timeline+metrics to the incident doc and assign owners for fixes.

maria: signing off. under control. :white_check_mark:
